measures: single-point acoustic Doppler water velocity, temperature, heading, tilt, pressure; optional PUV directional waves
claim: Velocity range user-selectable 1.0 to 5.0 m/s; accuracy +/-1% of measured value +/-0.5 cm/s; precision typ. 1 cm/s; cell size 0.75 m; temperature -4 to +40 degC at +/-0.1 degC; compass <2 deg; tilt 0.2 deg below 30 deg; pressure 0.5% FS; 500 m depth rating; RS-422 (inquire for RS-232) 9600 baud to 1.2 Mbaud; 16 GB memory; 9-24 VDC, peak 4.5 A; max sampling rate 1 Hz.
notes: Manufacturer. Suitability for this application VERIFIED for the current forcing channel only; it constrains no chemistry. Endurance in months is unknown: no duty-cycle table was retrieved. Message formats on RS-422 are unknown; the integrator manual was not retrieved. A serial link is not an API.

measures: seabed-mounted acoustic Doppler current profile plus pressure-inverted-echosounder time of flight and sound velocity
claim: 62.5 kHz; profiling range 800+ m depending on water environment; 4,100 m depth rating; RS232, Ethernet and acoustic modem; integrated LMF 14-19 kHz modem and acoustic release; 504 Ah dual lithium primary battery, 6 weeks full rate or 2 years scheduled; outputs PD0, A gram, B gram simultaneously; Origin Portal embedded web UI, Origin Scheduler, Origin Viewer, Origin Topside; edge computing with customizable apps via a Software Development Kit.
notes: Manufacturer. Suitability for this application UNKNOWN and probably poor: 62.5 kHz is a long-range coarse-cell configuration and would resolve almost nothing in the demonstrator's 5 m mixing depth. Retained as the clearest verified example of a seabed instrument with Ethernet, an embedded web interface, an acoustic back channel and a published SDK.

model: Doppler Current Profiler Sensor 5400/5400P/5402/5403 and Doppler Current Sensor 4420/4520/4830/4930 family
measures: current speed and direction, sea temperature; acoustic waves on 5400P; built-in compass and tilt with motion compensation
claim: DCS speed range 0 to 300 cm/s; depth ratings 300 m (5400), 4500 m (5402), 6000 m (5403); output over serial or AiCap bus, with RS-232, AiCaP and RS-422 options depending on model; in-line ZPulse 5800 family can hold a load of up to 1300 kg.
notes: Manufacturer. Accuracy, power and deployment duration are unknown from the page retrieved. AiCaP is a proprietary CANbus protocol and is not an application-level API. Suitability for this application UNKNOWN until the TD 304 operating manual is read.

claim: 15 mm x 46 mm, max diameter 17 mm; alumina ceramic housing; 19 g in air, 12 g in water; 12 bit resolution; temperature -2 to +40 degC, resolution 0.032 degC, accuracy +/-0.1 degC, 63% response in 20 s; depth ranges 0.1-50, 0.1-100, 1-270, 5-800, 5-1500, 10-3000 m; depth resolution 0.03% and accuracy +/-0.6% of selected range; EEPROM 174,000 measurements, option 524,068; minimum interval 0.1 s, burst 10 Hz, up to 7 intervals; requires PC Communication Cable and SeaStar Windows software.
notes: Manufacturer. Iceland is European non-EU (EEA). Suitability VERIFIED for a cheap redundant per-tile temperature and depth record. NO in-water protocol at all: data are read out over a PC cable after recovery, so available_at_utc equals the recovery time, not the observation time. A reported 9 year battery life at a 10 minute interval is SEARCH_INDEX_ONLY and unverified.

measures: conductivity, salinity and temperature by inductive ring-coil method
claim: Conductivity ranges from 0 to 100 mS/cm; Modbus RS-485 and SDI12 digital communication; IP68; low maintenance and consumable-free technology; resistant to fouling.
notes: Manufacturer, Champigny-sur-Marne. Accuracy, power supply and pressure or depth rating are unknown from the page retrieved. IP68 is not a deployment depth. Register map unknown. 100 mS/cm covers full-strength seawater at about 53 mS/cm. Suitability UNKNOWN pending a depth rating; context and QC channel only, never a metal channel.

model: Digital sensor PHEHT (PHEHT and PHT monobloc)
claim: pH 0.00 to 14.00; redox -1000 to +1000 mV; temperature 0 to +50.00 degC; Modbus RS-485 digital communication; changeable Plastogel cartridge; calibration and history stored in the sensor.
notes: Manufacturer. Accuracy not published on the manufacturer page; unknown. Third-party listings state SDI-12 as well as Modbus, 5-12 V supply, maximum 5 bar and IP68; those are SEARCH_INDEX_ONLY and unverified. Seawater pH needs a total-scale calibration and no seawater accuracy statement was found. Redox in sediment is operationally defined and poorly reproducible. Suitability UNKNOWN; context and QC only.

measures: turbidity by 90 degree infrared light-scattering nephelometry, suspended solids, medium temperature
claim: Turbidity 0 to 4000 NTU over four automatically selected ranges; suspended solids 0 to 4500 mg/L; Modbus RTU RS485 and SDI-12; IP68; optional HYDROCLEAN automatic cleaning system.
notes: Manufacturer. Accuracy and pressure or depth rating unknown from the page retrieved. ISO 7027 compliance appears only in third-party listings (SEARCH_INDEX_ONLY). Turbidity carries no metal information whatever and must never be used to infer chemistry (AGENTS.md rule 5). Suitability UNKNOWN pending a depth rating.

measures: nothing directly; it is a compact carrier and logger for the manufacturer's WiMo smart sensors
claim: Modbus communication; 9-16 VDC power input with very low power consumption; tool-free sensor connection with calibration values retained in the sensor; all WiMo smart sensors can be connected; user manual available on request.
notes: Manufacturer, 6 rue Gutenberg, ZI Kerandre, 56700 Hennebont, ISO 9001:2015 stated. Depth rating, register map, function codes, framing, logging capacity and any SDK are all unknown. An embedded configuration interface is not a public API. Which WiMo sensors are available was not established. Suitability UNKNOWN.

measures: anodic stripping voltammetry at a mercury-plated iridium gel-integrated microelectrode array; analytes Cu, Pb, Cd, Zn as the dynamic or labile fraction
claim: Peer-reviewed review states the VIP 'has been developed by Geneva University and commercialized by Idronaut for more than two decades' and that 'The VIP/TracMetal provides nice analytical performances in seawater or estuarine conditions due to the high salinity, constant pHs and small NOM concentrations'.
notes: Manufacturer. THE MERCURY IN THIS INSTRUMENT IS THE WORKING ELECTRODE, NOT THE ANALYTE: it is not a mercury sensor. Every manufacturer URL failed TLS certificate verification on 2026-09-08 (https://www.idronaut.it/, /research-projects/, and /wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Vip-Leaflet.pdf), so current orderability is NOT established. Detection limit in any matrix unknown; cycle time unknown; consumables unknown; unattended benthic duration unknown. Suitability UNKNOWN.

model: 884 Professional VA with Bi drop electrode, Application Bulletin 438/1
measures: cadmium and lead by anodic stripping voltammetry in acetate buffer at pH 4.6, quantified by two standard additions
claim: The limit of detection is 0.1 microgram/L for Cd and 0.5 microgram/L for Pb, with a 60 s deposition time and a working range of 0.1-15 microgram/L Cd and 0.5-15 microgram/L Pb. Samples listed: tap water, mineral water, and sea water. The bulletin states: 'This method is best suited for tap water and mineral water samples.' In the results table, sea water reads < LOD for Pb and THE SPIKED SEA-WATER LEAD ROW IS BLANK; spiked sea-water cadmium recovered at 82%.
notes: Manufacturer. Laboratory benchtop only, not submersible: 10 mL sample plus 1 mL electrolyte, 5 min purge, standard additions, optional 90 min UV digestion at 90 degC. NOT SUITABLE as published for sea-water lead. This record is the cleanest available proof that a published fresh-water LOD is not a sea-water performance figure. Other Metrohm methods (scTRACE Gold, screen-printed electrodes) were not evaluated.

measures: total mercury by thermal decomposition, gold amalgamation and double-beam atomic absorption spectrophotometry, with no sample preparation
claim: Compliance with EPA Method 7473, ASTM D-6722-01 and D-7623-10; solids, liquids and gases accepted without pre-treatment; analysis time about 5 to 6 minutes; ppt-level quantification. A detection limit as low as 0.0003 ng with a range to 30,000 ng appears in SEARCH_INDEX_ONLY sources only.
notes: Manufacturer, but the evidence URL is a third-party equipment directory reproducing manufacturer information, not the manufacturer's own page. Both manufacturer routes failed on 2026-09-08: https://www.milestonesci.com/direct-mercury-analyzer/ returned HTTP 403, and milestonesrl.com URLs failed TLS certificate verification. A mass detection limit converts to a concentration only through the sample size, so the concentration limit in a sea-water matrix is unknown and should be assumed unreachable without preconcentration. Plausible for retrieved-media solid assay; not established for water. Not a methylmercury method.

measures: total mercury by vapour generation and atomic fluorescence spectrometry with an on-board gold pre-concentration trap
claim: SEARCH_INDEX_ONLY: developed for compliance with EPA Method 1631; 'typically used for water samples where a detection limit below 0.05ppt is required'; 'routine detection limits of 0.01ppt' achievable. The matrix in which those limits apply is NOT established.
notes: Manufacturer. Every retrieval route attempted on 2026-09-08 returned HTTP 403, including http://psanalytical.com/elements/hg and the deep product URL already recorded in docs/REFERENCES.md [S21]. This repeats the failure noted in the previous snapshot, so the situation has not improved. Laboratory bench instrument, not submersible. Ultra-trace mercury results are dominated by sampling and preservation, not by the instrument. Suitability UNKNOWN.

model: LSPM-NP, loaded DGT device for metals (cationic) in sediment using a Chelex binding layer
measures: time-integrated accumulated mass of cationic metals onto a Chelex binding layer behind a 0.8 mm APA diffusive gel and a polyethersulphone filter membrane
claim: Can measure up to 30 metals, including Cd, Co, Cu, Fe, Mn, Ni, Pb, Zn. Standard sediment holder with 0.8 mm APA diffusive gel, polyethersulphone filter membrane and Chelex binding layer. Listed price GBP 73.00 on the manufacturer page on the access date.
notes: Manufacturer, Summer Cottage, Cockerham Road, Bay Horse, Lancaster LA2 0HF. MERCURY IS NOT LISTED among the metals; a Hg DGT needs a different binding layer and whether one is sold was not established. Reports ACCUMULATED MASS over a window, never a point concentration; the fraction is DGT-labile and is operationally different from voltammetric labile. Requires retrieval, elution and instrumental analysis in a laboratory. Deployment duration and seawater salinity limits unknown at vendor level. The listed price is a published list price, not a quotation, and excludes shipping, analysis and tax. Suitability VERIFIED as the time-integrated porewater lead channel.

measures: in-situ benthic chamber incubation with microsensors in the lid: O2, H2, N2O, pH and H2S
claim: Continuous deployment down to 300 m, optionally deep-sea deployment down to 6,000 m; powerful Field DataLogger; system programming via a PC software interface; ready for optodes and RS-232 devices; lid closes and measurements start for chamber incubation.
notes: Manufacturer. THE SENSOR SET CONTAINS NO Pb AND NO Hg CHANNEL. A metal flux would require timed water sub-samples during the incubation plus laboratory analysis, which is a different workflow from the electrodes sold with it. Chamber enclosed area and volume are NOT stated on the page retrieved, and without an area no areal flux can be computed (see ObservationRecord.chamber_area_m2). Deployment duration and power unknown. A chamber alters local hydrodynamics and can suppress the advective seepage it is meant to measure. Suitability UNKNOWN for metals as sold, and this is the highest-value open question in the whole matrix.

model: Rhizon CSS (standard Rhizon family: SMS, MOM, CSS, Flex; also MacroRhizon and MicroRhizon)
measures: nothing directly; it extracts porewater under vacuum through a hydrophilic microporous polymer tube for laboratory analysis
claim: Standard Rhizons: outer diameter 2.5 mm, membrane length 5 cm or 10 cm, pore sizes 0.15 and 0.60 micrometres. Application: sampling pore water in pots, vessels, cylinders or columns filled with settled soil, or in undisturbed cores and sediments. MacroRhizon 4.5 mm with female luer lock; MicroRhizon 1.2 mm outer diameter, 8 mm membrane, 0.15 micrometre pore size, steam-sterilisable.
notes: Manufacturer per the site copyright; town and full address unknown from the page retrieved. No protocol, no power, no telemetry. Yields a filtered dissolved fraction whose cut-off is the membrane pore size, so it maps to Fraction.DISSOLVED_FILTERED and not to LABILE or DGT_LABILE. Trace-metal blank behaviour for Pb and Hg through the polymer and luer fitting was NOT evaluated; do not assume clean trace-metal performance. In-situ seabed deployment through a mat is unknown. Suitability VERIFIED as a porewater extraction method subject to a blank study; this is the channel that constrains C_sed.

model: Gaps M5 USBL (family: Gaps M3, M5, M7)
measures: ultra-short-baseline acoustic position of a subsea transponder, with embedded fibre-optic-gyroscope inertial navigation, plus acoustic telemetry
claim: Gaps M5: 995 m or 4,000 m operating range variants; absolute accuracy 0.06% of slant range (CEP50); 200 degree aperture with above-horizontal tracking; true calibration-free operation with an embedded Phins FOG-based INS; third-party transponder compatible; acoustic telemetry for message transmission, INS re-alignment and sensor data retrieval.
notes: Manufacturer. Output formats, interfaces and any SDK are unknown from the page retrieved. Accuracy is a percentage of slant range; at a 20 m coastal deployment the practical accuracy is dominated by sound-speed error, multipath off the seabed and transponder mounting, none of which the headline figure captures. Whether it can resolve the centimetre-to-decimetre tile displacement that Parameter.MAT_DISPLACEMENT needs is UNKNOWN. A short baseline or a mechanical tell-tale may serve better and was not researched.

measures: visual inspection: HD tilt camera 1920x1080, mechanical tilt -30 to +30 degrees, 115 degree vertical field of view; onboard depth (0-30 bar), temperature and 3-axis IMU
claim: 305 m / 1000 feet depth rating; operational in up to 2 knots current; endurance about 2 h standard battery or 5 h high-capacity battery; tether up to 300 m with 100 kg breaking strength; three guest ports supporting Ethernet, RS232, I2C, PWM and UART; Water Linked DVL A50 and acoustic positioning available as add-ons; the Blueye SDK is referenced.
notes: Manufacturer, Trondheim. A publicly maintained Python SDK on GitHub supporting custom payload control and mission scripting is reported by SEARCH_INDEX_ONLY sources; the repository was not retrieved and the licence is unknown. Produces categorical condition classes and lengths, never chemistry. Cannot see burial depth under sediment, cannot see saturation, cannot see fouling inside the layer. Visibility over a disturbed seabed will limit it before current does: the demonstrator's peak forcing is about 0.22 m/s against a 2 knot (about 1.03 m/s) capability. Suitability VERIFIED for ROV_INSPECTION condition channels.

model: Site Services: ROV inspection and survey services (equipment: Mini TORTUGA, TORTUGA standard and XP4; Catarob, AirCAT, Cat-Surveyor, SeaCAT USVs)
measures: position, geometry and visual condition: underwater inspection and measurement with ROVs, 3D photogrammetry and modelling, bathymetric survey with unmanned surface vessels
claim: Over 20 years of operations in France and internationally; more than 180 missions completed; over 80 public and private clients; multi-depth inspection ROVs, remote-controlled and autonomous USV catamarans, multibeam and side-scan sonars, thickness measurement sensors and HD cameras; equipment rental and operator training also offered.
notes: Manufacturer of its own ROVs and USVs AND a service provider, Marseille. NO reference to sediment remediation, capping or contaminated-site work was found on the page retrieved. Day rates, mobilisation costs, availability and repeat-survey positioning accuracy are all unknown. CostConfig.rov_survey_eur = 4200.0 in this repository remains an assumption and no quotation exists. Suitability UNKNOWN.

model: TracMetal multichannel submersible probe / Au-GIME Hg(II) sensor
measures: in-situ voltammetric determination of the potentially bioavailable fraction of Hg(II), As(III), Cd(II), Pb(II), Cu(II) and Zn(II) using Hg-plated and gold-nanofilament gel-integrated microelectrode arrays in a three-channel flow cell
claim: Mercury IS the analyte on the gold channel. Described in Tercier-Waeber et al. (2021), ACS Sensors 6(3):925-937, DOI 10.1021/acssensors.0c02111. Deployed in Arcachon Bay. A 2024 review reports that underwater in-situ continuous operation of such analysers has not exceeded 10 days (SEARCH_INDEX_ONLY).
notes: Research group, not a manufacturer or distributor. IT CANNOT BE ORDERED: no supplier, price, lead time or support arrangement was found. Detection limits unknown. Interface unknown. A pumped peristaltic flow cell on a multi-month benthic deployment is unproven. Recorded because it is the only verified evidence that in-situ dissolved Hg(II) measurement in seawater is physically possible, and because it is the correct citation when asked whether a continuous mercury sensor exists. The MDPI review at https://www.mdpi.com/2227-9040/12/8/158 returned HTTP 403 on the access date.
